title: Exact off-class global basin transfers to empirical exchange-stable optima
statement: Let X,Z be iid Uniform[-1,1], S_psi=X, S_lambda=3X^2-1+Z, and K=3. This atomless bounded law has E[S_lambda|shat=X]=3X^2-1 != 0, so it is outside class (L). The X-interval rule with cuts +/-1/3 is a regular DS17 root at beta=0 with I_q=diag(8/27,32/81), masses 1/3, projected separation 2/3, and Ds retention 8/9. It uniquely attains the population three-cell profiled optimum and is strictly isolated in decision distance. For iid equal-weight samples with no sample centering, every sequence of exact global finite regular profiled-Ds optima converges after relabeling to this rule in empirical decision distance and cell moments, hence is eventually ordinary one-point exchange-stable with fixed margins c0=1/4, kappa=1/4, gamma=1/2. This is an existence/global-selection theorem, not a claim that raw population-cut labels or practical exchange ascent are finite stable or basin-selecting.
assumptions: iid equal-weight empirical samples; scores are not sample-centered
exact global finite optima over nonempty regular labelings with I_lambda_lambda>0
cell labels are compared up to permutation

proof_location.section: DS18. Exact off-class global basin and empirical stable transfer

role: first proved off-(L) inhabitation and exact empirical-transfer instance for the DS17 gate
warning: Unaudited internal theorem. Transfer uses exact finite global optima; it does not prove persistence of a generic local root, stability of raw population labels, branch completeness, mix3 uniqueness, or selection by the practical exchange solver. No src/ compile surface is authorized before a fresh independent audit.
